dedupe_keys.name: tri city nutritional capability accessibility index ncai neighbourhood food access in hong kong singapore and seoul 2024 2025

description: This data set measures how easily residents of three very dense Asian cities can reach food outlets that support a healthy diet, neighbourhood by neighbourhood. The producer is Zhaojie Chen of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, for a comparative study of food insecurity in Hong Kong, Singapore and Seoul. Coverage is Hong Kong's 18 districts, Singapore's 241 inhabited planning subzones, using hawker centres and OpenStreetMap outlets, and Seoul's 426 administrative neighbourhoods, for 2024 to 2025. The Nutritional Capability Accessibility Index combines outlet supply, population demand and travel distance with an enhanced two-step floating catchment method, and the package gives the processed demographics and outlet counts, index scores with spatial clustering statistics, the Python scripts that fetch data and compute the index, and figures. It is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: a new composite index, differing spatial units between cities, and outlet lists that depend on open data completeness. Simulation uses: locating neighbourhoods with weak food access for emergency food distribution planning, and testing how closures of markets or hawker centres change access. Related records: the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) is a comparable national measure for the United States.

name: Tri-City Nutritional Capability Accessibility Index (NCAI): neighbourhood food access in Hong Kong, Singapore and Seoul (2024-2025)
schema_summary: Processed demographics and food outlet counts by district (Hong Kong, 18 districts), NCAI scores and spatial statistics by subzone (Singapore, 241 subzones, hawker centres and OpenStreetMap outlets) and by dong (Seoul, 426); Python scripts for data acquisition, Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA) accessibility, Moran's I and LISA; figures

sources.note: Creator Chen (Hong Kong Polytechnic University); CC BY 4.0; published 2026-04-25; Tri-City_NCAI_Dataset_v1.0.zip (4.6 MB); processed spatial, demographic and food-environment data for the manuscript 'Beyond Proximity: Nutritional Capability and the Spatial Architecture of Food Insecurity in Hyper-Dense High-Income Asian Cities'; NCAI at neighbourhood level: Hong Kong 18 District Council districts, Singapore 241 URA subzones, Seoul 426 dong; E2SFCA metrics, Moran's I and LISA; scripts 01_fetch_hk_data.py to 07_seoul_ncai_pipeline.py

title_en: Tri-City Nutritional Capability Accessibility Index (NCAI): neighbourhood food access in Hong Kong, Singapore and Seoul (2024-2025)
